evidence.field: 形義通解；graphic analysis and cited uses
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 星 as 晶 (a group of stars) plus 生 as phonetic, and says oracle forms add 生 as a sound marker. It reports star imagery and the star sense, an oracle-bone example 《合集》15625反 interpreted as clear weather, a Western Zhou bronze personal-name use in 麓伯簋, and Warring States/Qin and Han examples where 星 writes 腥. It links the clear-weather use to visible stars but notes the 《詩經》 reading is interpretive. These examples do not establish a complete chronology of senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：星

evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen account for 曐: “從晶，從生聲,” alongside an alternative pictographic explanation. It records 星 as a shortened form and lists 曐 and other historical variants. This documents the traditional dictionary account, not a settled reconstruction of the earliest graphic sequence.
evidence.title: [A01792] 星 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: discussion of 晶 and 星 paleography
evidence.text: The paper cites oracle forms of 晶 and 星, including 星 examples 合15637, 合11501, and 合40207, and identifies a Western Zhou bronze form from 麓伯簋. Its discussion gives a 晶-based pictographic explanation and notes the Shuowen form 从晶、生聲. This supports early form attestations but does not settle whether every earliest 星 form included 生 or whether a 晶-only spelling preceded it.
evidence.title: 中國學術年刊 第四十七期（春季號）

evidence.source: 國學大師字形演變 compilation
evidence.field: dated form labels and graphic interpretation
evidence.text: The page labels oracle forms with corpus references, lists the 麓伯星父簋 as Western Zhou bronze, and describes oracle 星 forms as star signs plus 生. It interprets later simplification as reducing 晶 to 日 while retaining 生. This account conflicts with a 晶-first/addition sequence in other accounts; the page does not resolve whether the claims concern different forms or different analyses.
evidence.title: 星字形演变字源

The rows are local data and were not verified here against an external table page; they do not by themselves prove 生’s phonetic role.

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the exact 星 oracle file description. Opened it and copied its Original file link; direct SVG retrieval was unsupported by the web viewer, but the exact image URL was supplied by the inspected link.
Search returned the Commons Star oracle file page; it corroborated Shang oracle-style identification, HB2813 source attribution and public-domain representation rights.

gaps: Early graphic accounts conflict: some describe a 晶-like star depiction with 生 already present in oracle forms, while other accounts treat a 晶-only spelling as earlier and 星 as adding 生. The consulted text sources do not resolve the sequence; no corruption or scribal error is established.

The cited oracle reading as clear weather is an interpretation, and the 《詩經》 phrase 星言夙駕 is disputed. These do not establish a secure first occurrence or complete chronology for the clear-weather sense. The documented Western Zhou bronze use is a personal name, not proof of first use for the star sense.

CUHK reports later graph borrowing for 腥 and scattered/numerous extensions, but intermediate semantic links and first occurrences for those extensions remain unestablished. No whole-graph phonetic-loan account is needed for the supported 生-component analysis.

The exact official Unicode lookups for U+661F and U+751F returned internal errors. Baxter–Sagart local rows were supplied, but the cited table page did not yield external verification of both exact rows in this invocation.
The Commons oracle asset is a modern SVG redraw. It is not a photograph of an oracle bone artifact. No pixels were visually inspected in this research stage.
No repository source reuse terms were verified for a versioned extract; the inspected sources support concise character-specific citations and paraphrases instead.
